      How it’s worked out
      The line
      Your file, read in the browser, one point every 25 m. Heights from the file; when it has none, from Open-Meteo’s 90 m elevation model. Heights are averaged over 125 m so barometer noise doesn’t count as climbing; climbing adds up only when the road rises 2 m or more.
      Climbs
      A climb starts where the grade over 200 m reaches 3% and ends where it drops below; a dip shorter than 300 m that doesn’t fall more than 2% stays part of the climb. Under 100 ft of gain it’s a rise, not a climb. Category is Strava’s rule: length in metres times average grade. 8,000 is cat 4, 16,000 cat 3, 32,000 cat 2, 64,000 cat 1, 80,000 HC.
      Times
      Your flat speed, slower on the climbs (divided by 1 + 0.12 × grade), faster on the descents (up to 1.35×). An estimate. No stops are counted; add your coffee.
      Weather
      Open-Meteo’s hourly forecast at up to eight points: the start, every twelve miles, the foot of each climb, the finish, each at the hour you get there. Headwind means the wind is coming from within 45° of where you’re heading; tailwind, from behind; everything else is a crosswind. Nine days out or less; beyond that there’s no forecast worth printing.
      Wear and water
      A house table by temperature: winter kit under 40°F, warmers under 60, summer kit over 70, sun sleeves and an early start over 90. Water is about a bottle an hour at 80°F, one and a half at 90, two over 100, and over 100 isn’t an afternoon ride.
      Difficulty
      Hard: 60 miles or more, 100 ft of climbing a mile or more, or 40 miles at 60 ft a mile. Moderate: 25 miles or 50 ft a mile. Easy: the rest.
      What leaves your browser
      Nothing but the sample coordinates in the two Open-Meteo requests. No account, no cookies, nothing stored. The share link carries the route itself, so it works for anyone.

      I’d like to say I ride for everyone else. I ride because it changed me.

      In 2027 I ride 10,000 miles, all on the bike, and every ride gets written down. The money goes through the orgs’ own rides. It never touches me.
